digest.headline: The Nasdaq 100 registered its worst month since March 2025 as a tech sell-off deepened and OpenAI trimmed its IPO valuation target.

lede.b: The Nasdaq 100 index, which is a group of one hundred large technology companies traded on the stock market, recorded its worst month since March 2025 following a sharp tech sell-off. A sell-off means many investors are trying to sell their shares at the same time, which causes prices to drop. OpenAI, an artificial intelligence company, responded to this broader market correction by lowering its initial public offering valuation target by $150bn. An initial public offering is when a private company first sells shares to the public. Meanwhile, a stealth bear market deepened as 60% of S&P 500 stocks dropped by 20% or more from their peaks. The S&P 500 is a stock market index tracking five hundred of the largest companies in the United States. Four individual S&P 500 stocks touched 52-week lows on Friday.
lede.i: The Nasdaq 100 registered its worst month since March 2025 following a sharp tech sell-off across equities. OpenAI trimmed its IPO valuation target by $150bn in response to the broader market correction. Simultaneously, a stealth bear market deepened as 60% of S&P 500 stocks dropped by 20% or more from their peaks. Four individual S&P 500 stocks touched 52-week lows on Friday.
lede.a: The Nasdaq 100 recorded its worst monthly performance since March 2025 amid a systemic tech correction. OpenAI recalibrated its IPO valuation target downward by $150bn in direct response to compressed valuation multiples. Parallel to this contraction, the broader S&P 500 exhibited stealth bear market characteristics as 60% of its constituent equities declined by 20% or more from their cyclical peaks. Four individual S&P 500 equities printed 52-week lows on Friday.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US markets register tech sell-offs and S&P 500 lows

stories.t: Tech Sell-Off Hits Nasdaq 100 and Valuation Targets
stories.b: The Nasdaq 100 index, which tracks one hundred large technology companies, just finished its worst month since March 2025. This drop follows a brutal sell-off in technology shares. OpenAI responded to this market slide by reportedly trimming its initial public offering valuation target by $150bn.
stories.i: The Nasdaq 100 registered its worst month since March 2025 following a brutal tech sell-off. OpenAI trimmed its IPO valuation target by $150bn in response to the broader market correction.
stories.a: The Nasdaq 100 printed its worst monthly performance since March 2025 amid a systemic tech sell-off. Subsequent valuation adjustments forced OpenAI to slash its IPO target by $150bn, testing primary market appetite.

stories.t: Stealth Bear Market Deepens Across S&P 500 Stocks
stories.b: A bear market is a period when stock prices fall significantly, usually by twenty percent or more. This stealth bear market worsened as sixty percent of all stocks in the S&P 500 index dropped by twenty percent or more. Separately, four individual S&P 500 stocks hit new fifty-two-week lows on Friday.
stories.i: The stealth bear market deepened as 60% of S&P 500 stocks dropped by 20% or more from their peaks. Meanwhile, 4 individual S&P 500 stocks touched 52-week lows on Friday.
stories.a: Breadth deterioration intensified within the S&P 500 as 60% of index constituents crossed the 20% drawdown threshold from recent highs. Concurrently, 4 S&P 500 equities registered fresh 52-week lows on Friday.

politics.b: Government officials made no new policy announcements regarding the falling stock prices today.
politics.i: Federal policymakers refrained from issuing emergency statements during the tech sector sell-off.
politics.a: Executive branch officials maintained standard silence as public equity indices experienced broad drawdowns.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England mortgage limits and budget confidence drop

stories.t: Bank of England Examines Riskier Lending Limits
stories.b: The Bank of England is the country's central bank, which is the main bank that oversees all other banks and sets the rules for the financial system. Officials are looking at raising the high-risk mortgage threshold. A mortgage is a large loan used to buy a home. This change would ease limits on riskier mortgage lending. The Financial Times reported the review.
stories.i: The Bank of England explores raising the threshold for high-risk mortgage lending. Officials consider easing a key limit on riskier loans. The Financial Times disclosed the policy review regarding these risk metrics.
stories.a: The Bank of England weighs adjustments to macroprudential guardrails surrounding leveraged property exposures. The institution evaluates lifting the ceiling on high-risk mortgage origination limits, as reported by the Financial Times. Financial stability frameworks face calibration shifts if lenders expand balance sheet allocations toward more volatile housing debt.

stories.t: Institute of Directors Reports Confidence Drop
stories.b: British business confidence has dropped after the release of the recent government spending plan. The Institute of Directors published the drop. Companies are reacting to the financial measures announced by officials.
stories.i: British business confidence falls following the release of Budget 2026. The Institute of Directors registers the sentiment decline among corporate leaders. Survey data captures the immediate commercial reaction to the fiscal announcements.
stories.a: Corporate sentiment contracts across the British economy in the wake of Budget 2026. The Institute of Directors documents the deterioration in forward-looking business confidence indicators. Commercial leadership reassesses operational expenditure frameworks following the fiscal disclosures.

politics.b: The government released a new budget that has changed tax rules for private pensions and household finances. Families report that the financial changes will cost them extra money each year. Business leaders also report lower confidence after the announcements.
politics.i: Budget 2026 introduces fiscal adjustments affecting private pension tax treatment and household incomes. Taxpayers calculate increased annual costs following the legislative package. The Institute of Directors notes a corresponding contraction in commercial sentiment.
politics.a: Fiscal policy adjustments enacted in Budget 2026 alter the taxation of private pension distributions and household revenue streams. Private analyses estimate substantial annual cost increases for individual taxpayers. Commercial sentiment indicators register immediate strain as corporate leadership absorbs the regulatory shifts.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German inflation cools and the DAX slips

stories.t: German Price Growth Slows as the DAX Drops
stories.b: The rate at which prices rise in Germany, known as inflation, got slower recently. The main stock market index in Germany, called the DAX, fell in value anyway. An index is a group of shares tracked together to show how a market is doing. Share prices move for many different reasons beyond just price changes in the broader economy. The DAX slipped despite the cooler economic figures.
stories.i: German inflation slowed down over the period. The DAX index dropped in response to wider market pressures. Stock indices reflect overall corporate valuations rather than moving in lockstep with consumer price metrics. Equity markets often pull back even when macro data shows easing price pressures.
stories.a: German headline inflation printed lower, yet the DAX drifted downward. Equity valuations disconnected from the benign macro print due to sector-specific rotations. Index constituents absorbed localized selling pressure that outweighed the broader easing in consumer price growth.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Bank of Japan declares inflation win and corporate income peaks

stories.t: Bank of Japan Targets Interest Rates After Reaching Goal
stories.src: Wall Street Journal · The Japan News
stories.b: The Bank of Japan is the main bank that runs the country's money system. It sets rules for borrowing. It has reached its 2% goal for inflation, which is when the prices of everyday items go up over time. This success clears the way for the bank to raise interest rates, which are extra charges on loans. The bank now focuses on keeping this progress going.
stories.i: The Bank of Japan declared that its 2% inflation target has been reached. This milestone clears the path for future rate hikes by the central bank. Policymakers now shift their operational focus toward sustaining these price levels over time.
stories.a: The Bank of Japan officially acknowledged the attainment of its 2% price stability objective, removing the primary constraint against normalization. Real-rate dynamics now permit policy tightening as authorities pivot from targeting generation to managing persistence. Market participants price the transition path under the assumption that terminal rate expectations will anchor around newly established stability parameters.

stories.t: Japanese Corporate Income Reaches Record High
stories.b: Japanese companies made a record amount of money in the 2025 financial year. Total corporate income hit 118 trillion yen. This massive earnings report covers all businesses across the country. The data shows strong financial health for firms operating in Japan.
stories.i: Japanese corporate income reached a record 118 trillion yen in fiscal year 2025. This peak reflects broad-based earnings growth across the nation's corporate sector. The figures provide a robust backdrop for domestic business expansion.
stories.a: Japanese corporate income printed at an all-time high of 118 trillion yen for fiscal year 2025. Margin expansion and pricing power drove aggregate profitability past historical boundaries. Equity analysts incorporate these cash generation metrics into valuation models for domestic cyclical sectors.

stories.t: Hon Hai Acquires Stake in Mitsubishi Electric Unit
stories.b: Hon Hai is buying a 50% stake in Mitsubishi Electric Mobile. The deal costs 115 billion yen. Both companies will run the automotive equipment business together. The partnership focuses on car parts and technology.
stories.i: Hon Hai agreed to acquire a 50% stake in Mitsubishi Electric Mobile for 115 billion yen. The two firms will jointly operate the automotive equipment business following the transaction. This partnership targets the global vehicle component market.
stories.a: Hon Hai secured a 50% equity interest in Mitsubishi Electric Mobile via a 115 billion yen capital outlay. Joint operational control of the automotive equipment business creates a new vertical integration conduit. Synergies depend on harmonizing manufacturing footprints across regional supply chains.

politics.i: Foreign caregivers in Japan face an examination hurdle as their official grace period concludes. Regulatory compliance now requires passing the mandatory credentialing test.
politics.a: Foreign caregivers confront immediate attrition risks as the statutory grace period for qualification exams expires. Labor supply constraints in the eldercare sector tighten as non-compliant workers face disqualification.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate earnings and new delivery routes emerge

stories.t: Corporate Earnings and AI Toys Surge
stories.b: An artificial intelligence toy market in China grew by 183.9% compared to the same time last year. Meanwhile, 2,904 companies listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange posted a combined net profit of 1.08 trillion yuan for the third quarter. Out of those firms, 433 doubled their profits. GAC Group reported a revenue of 75.156 billion yuan for the first three quarters, marking a 12.29% increase.
stories.i: Artificial intelligence toy sales in China expanded by 183.9% year on year. Across the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, 2,904 companies reported a combined net profit of 1.08 trillion yuan for the third quarter, with 433 businesses doubling their earnings. GAC Group recorded 75.156 billion yuan in revenue for the first three quarters, representing a 12.29% rise driven by exports and own brands.
stories.a: Sales of artificial intelligence toys in China advanced 183.9% year on year according to recent data. Third-quarter filings on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange showed 2,904 companies generating a combined net profit of 1.08 trillion yuan, with 433 entities doubling profits. GAC Group posted 75.156 billion yuan in revenue for the first three quarters, up 12.29% on the back of brand expansion and export growth.

stories.t: New Drone Routes and Industrial Investments
stories.b: Guizhou launched its very first campus low-altitude drone delivery route. Wuxi broke ground on a new new energy vehicle parts project with a total investment of 600 million yuan. Juqiao Industrial completed 100 million yuan in Series A financing through a round led by Ant Group.
stories.i: Guizhou introduced its first campus low-altitude drone delivery route. Wuxi initiated construction on a new energy vehicle parts project backed by a 600 million yuan total investment. Juqiao Industrial secured 100 million yuan in Series A financing in a round led by Ant Group.
stories.a: Guizhou established its inaugural campus low-altitude drone delivery route. Wuxi commenced construction on a new energy vehicle parts facility supported by a 600 million yuan total investment. Juqiao Industrial closed a 100 million yuan Series A financing round led by Ant Group.

politics.b: Chery reported that its revenue for the first three quarters rose 12% to reach 241.2 billion yuan. An executive stated that the overseas target is to grow by another 20% next year.
politics.i: Chery posted a 12% increase in first-quarter-to-third-quarter revenue, reaching 241.2 billion yuan. An executive announced an overseas growth target of 20% for the following year.
politics.a: Chery disclosed a 12% rise in revenue to 241.2. billion yuan across the first three quarters. Management outlined an overseas expansion target of 20% growth for the subsequent year.

India.label: India
India.sub: Indian equities rise led by healthcare as currency stays flat

stories.t: Healthcare and Pharma Drive Nifty and Sensex Higher
stories.b: The Nifty stock index went up by 2.59%. The Sensex stock index went up by 1.83%. Pharmaceutical and healthcare companies led these market gains. Stock indexes are baskets of shares that track how a group of companies performs.
stories.i: The Nifty rose by 2.59% and the Sensex climbed by 1.83%. Pharma and healthcare sectors spearheaded the upward movement. Investors rotated capital into these segments during the trading session.
stories.a: The Nifty advanced 2.59% while the Sensex added 1.83%, driven by outperformance in pharma and healthcare equities. Broad-based sectoral buying lifted the benchmark gauges. Momentum indicators point to continued focus on defensive groupings.

stories.t: Rupee Stabilises Against Brent Crude Pressures
stories.b: The Indian rupee currency stayed flat at 94.95 against the dollar. Brent crude oil priced at $117.84 per barrel capped weekly price moves. Currencies are the money systems used by different countries.
stories.i: The rupee settled flat at 94.95. Brent crude at $117.84 per barrel contained weekly currency fluctuations. Energy import costs remain a core metric for external inflation stability.
stories.a: The rupee closed unchanged at 94.95. Brent crude settling at $117.84 per barrel constrained broader weekly volatility bands. Macro desks continue to price energy-linked vulnerability into spot FX projections.

politics.b: The International Monetary Fund warned about super El Niño weather risks hurting the Indian economy. The IMF also noted the rupee acts as a first line of defence against energy shocks.

politics.a: The IMF flagged super El Niño meteorological risks for the broader macroeconomic trajectory. Policymakers view the local currency as the initial shock absorber against imported energy price spikes.

stories.t: Petrobras reports third oil discovery in the Amapá block
stories.src: Oil & Gas Middle East · Latin Times · Energy Intelligence
stories.b: Petrobras is a big Brazilian oil company. It finished drilling at the Morpho site and found a third oil discovery in the Amapá block. This discovery adds fuel to the climate debate in Brazil just before the COP30 meeting.
stories.i: Petrobras finished drilling operations at the Morpho site. The state-controlled company secured its third oil discovery in the Amapá block. The find intensifies domestic climate versus oil debates ahead of COP30.
stories.a: Petrobras completed Morpho well drilling operations to register its third hydrocarbons find in the Amapá block. The discovery sharpens the domestic climate versus fossil fuel debate immediately ahead of the COP30 summit.

stories.t: Petrobras refiners run at high utilization rates in October
stories.b: A company director stated that company refineries ran at 98% capacity during October. Wall Street analysts also lifted the stock to a strong buy rating.
stories.i: Company directors confirmed that refineries operated at 98% capacity through October. Meanwhile, Wall Street analysts upgraded the equity to a strong-buy rating.

politics.a: The latest offshore hydrocarbon discovery complicates domestic energy strategy. The timing heightens the climate versus oil policy debate immediately ahead of COP30.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco pricing changes, security incidents, and projects

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Adjusts Prices and Targets Infrastructure Expansion
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is a very large oil company owned by the government of Saudi Arabia. It just raised its official prices for liquefied petroleum gas, which is a type of gas used for heating and cooking, by 5.9% to 6.8%. At the same time, the company is looking at new business opportunities as Pakistan makes plans for a major oil hub in Balochistan. AMPO Poyam Valves also secured an order for offshore valves to be used at the Zuluf field development.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco increased official liquefied petroleum gas prices by 5.9% to 6.8%. The state-backed energy producer is evaluating new prospects as Pakistan progresses with plans for a large oil hub in Balochistan. Meanwhile, AMPO Poyam Valves secured an offshore equipment contract for the Zuluf field development.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco raised official liquefied petroleum gas pricing by 5.9% to 6.8%. The conglomerate is concurrently assessing participation parameters in Pakistan's planned Balochistan petroleum hub. Upstream supply chains advanced further with AMPO Poyam Valves securing an offshore contract for the Zuluf field development.

stories.t: Security Incidents Impact Saudi Infrastructure and Markets
stories.b: A recent Houthi attack on the airport in Riyadh resulted in 13 deaths, and the group also claimed responsibility for strikes targeting Saudi Aramco facilities. State news agencies reported that separate attacks cut Saudi oil output and slowed the flow along the East-West pipeline. Amid these security events, Saudi Arabia and Iran are currently holding talks.
stories.i: A strike attributed to the Houthi movement struck Riyadh airport, causing 13 fatalities alongside claimed hits on Saudi Aramco infrastructure. State news reports confirmed that attacks reduced national crude output and disrupted flow along the East-West pipeline. Diplomatic channels between Saudi Arabia and Iran remain active alongside these developments.
stories.a: A reported Houthi kinetic strike on Riyadh airport resulted in 13 casualties and claimed infrastructure impacts on Saudi Aramco assets. State media disclosures verified that attacks constrained aggregate petroleum output and throttled throughput on the East-West pipeline. Bilateral talks between Saudi Arabia and Iran are proceeding concurrently.

politics.b: Saudi Arabia and Iran are holding talks following recent security incidents. A strike hit the airport in Riyadh, causing 13 deaths.
politics.i: Diplomatic engagement is underway between Saudi Arabia and Iran following a Houthi strike on Riyadh airport that resulted in 13 fatalities.
politics.a: Bilateral communications between Saudi Arabia and Iran are ongoing in the wake of the kinetic strike on Riyadh airport attributed to the Houthi movement.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira exchange rates and public debt debates in Nigeria

stories.t: Naira Exchange Rates Shift at Markets
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. One dollar traded at N1,346.91 at the official market on October 31, 2026. Unofficial street markets priced the same dollar at N1,385. The official rate closed the month at N1,346 per dollar, reversing three months of gains.
stories.i: The official foreign exchange market priced the naira at N1,346.91 per dollar on October 31, 2026. Parallel market rates traded the dollar slightly higher at N1,385. Monthly figures show the currency closing October at N1,346 per dollar, erasing three months of prior gains.
stories.a: Spot pricing for the naira settled at N1,346.91 per dollar on the official window as October 31, 2026 concluded. Unofficial channels quoted the greenback at N1,385. Monthly aggregate data confirms the currency ending October at N1,346 per dollar, completely reversing the preceding three-month appreciation trend.

stories.t: Debate Erupts Over National Borrowing
stories.b: Former leaders and current officials are arguing about government loans. President Tinubu defended borrowing by saying that borrowing is not leprosy. Former leader Olusegun Obasanjo rejected this remark on October 31, 2026. Obasanjo stated that debt is actually worse than leprosy.
stories.i: Public disagreement emerged regarding federal borrowing strategies on October 31, 2026. President Tinubu previously defended taking on debt by stating that borrowing is not leprosy. Former leader Olusegun Obasanjo publicly criticized this stance, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy.
stories.a: National discourse centered on fiscal leverage following conflicting statements from the presidency and former leadership on October 31, 2026. President Tinubu defended state liabilities with the assertion that borrowing is not leprosy. Former head of state Olusegun Obasanjo repudiated the comparison, arguing instead that debt remains worse than leprosy.

politics.b: Political figures traded arguments about national debt and economic management on October 31, 2026. President Tinubu defended government borrowing. Former leader Olusegun Obasanjo criticized that defense.
politics.i: Political friction intensified on October 31, 2026, as former leader Olusegun Obasanjo rebuked President Tinubu over official borrowing policies. The exchange highlighted ongoing domestic divisions regarding fiscal policy and debt sustainability.
politics.a: Political capital diverged around fiscal orthodoxy on October 31, 2026, following Olusegun Obasanjo's direct rebuke of President Tinubu's debt defense. The public disagreement underscores polarized viewpoints within the political establishment regarding sovereign debt accumulation.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Housing operator takeovers and company updates drive equities

stories.t: Housing Operator Takeover Bids Draw Market Focus
stories.b: Takeover offers challenge listed housing operators in Australia. A takeover is when one company buys most of another company. This creates intense capital battles in the market. Investors watch these deals closely as bigger firms try to buy smaller ones.
stories.i: Takeover offers challenge listed housing operators across Australia. Capital battles heat up as acquirers target the sector. These corporate bids drive consolidation among property-related equities.
stories.a: Takeover offers challenge listed housing operators as capital battles intensify. Bidders target sector assets amid shifting valuation metrics. These corporate maneuvers compress spreads across competing bids.

stories.t: Fleetwood Sales Rise Countered by Share Price Decline
stories.b: Fleetwood shares slid even though sales rose. A share is a small piece of ownership in a company. Sometimes a company sells more goods, but investors still sell their shares. The stock price dropped despite the higher sales figures.
stories.i: Fleetwood shares slid even though sales rose. Equity markets punished the stock despite the top-line growth. Investors recalibrated expectations downward despite the positive sales report.
stories.a: Fleetwood shares slid even though sales rose during the period. Price action decoupled from the revenue expansion. Margin compression or guidance details likely drove the equity lower despite the top-line beat.

politics.i: Macro political updates remained absent from today's equity disclosures. Market participants focused exclusively on corporate earnings and asset valuations. Regulatory announcements played no primary role in the session.
politics.a: Fiscal and legislative updates did not feature in the session's data flow. Price discovery remained anchored to firm-specific fundamentals and corporate actions. Macro sovereign drivers exerted negligible influence on equity flows.
